name: Google for Developers — What is Machine Learning?
supportedFacts: ML uses data to train models; supervised, unsupervised and generative learning; numeric prediction versus content generation.

name: Google for Developers — Introduction to Large Language Models
supportedFacts: Language models learn text patterns and predict token sequences; tokens need not equal complete words.

name: Microsoft Learn — Prompt engineering techniques
supportedFacts: Prompt components include instructions, source content, context and examples; useful for specifying and reviewing tasks.

name: OpenAI Help Center — What is ChatGPT?
supportedFacts: Conversational assistant context and the need to check inaccurate or misleading responses. Outdated model-generation, cutoff and internet-access statements are not used.

name: Google — Gemini Apps Privacy Hub
supportedFacts: Data handling is service-specific; practice uses fictional data and makes no fixed claims about account settings.

name: Google — Create a notebook in Gemini Notebook
supportedFacts: Current notebook documentation includes supplied sources, questions about sources and generated notes/study-guide outputs. Playlist uses the older Notebook LM topic name.

name: Microsoft Learn — Text to speech overview
supportedFacts: Text-to-speech converts written text to synthesized speech. The course does not require Azure accounts or paid resources.

name: UNESCO — Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
supportedFacts: Human oversight, transparency and fairness as AI ethics principles; no expert certification or legal determination claimed.

name: Suno — Does Suno own the music I make?
supportedFacts: The provider distinguishes conditions according to the creation-time subscription plan. This supports checking actual terms, not a general copyright or ownership conclusion.
